about.text: AFCAT, where the relevant Ground Duty branch is notified and the candidate meets its eligibility requirements

about.label: Work environment
about.text: Air Force stations, logistics units, administrative offices, operational support units and headquarters

about.label: Career type
about.text: Military administration, personnel management, logistics, resource coordination and operational support

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: AFCAT eligibility differs between Ground Duty (Non-Technical) and Ground Duty (Technical) branches. Administration and Logistics generally fall under Ground Duty (Non-Technical), but the specific vacancies, educational qualifications, age limits, commission type and selection requirements must be verified from the applicable Indian Air Force notification.

AFCAT is a competitive entry route for eligible graduates. Selection typically involves the applicable written examination, Air Force selection assessments, medical examination and final merit/allocation procedures. Passing one stage does not guarantee final selection.

sections.heading: What Does a Ground Duty Officer (Administration / Logistics) Do?

blocks.text: A Ground Duty Officer supports the operational readiness of the Indian Air Force through administration, personnel coordination, resource management and logistics.
Administration and Logistics are related but distinct functions.

blocks.label: Administration
blocks.text: Personnel administration, station services, discipline-related processes, organizational coordination and assigned administrative responsibilities.

blocks.label: Logistics
blocks.text: Supply-chain coordination, inventory management, procurement support, equipment availability, storage, distribution and movement of resources.
Depending on the branch and posting, responsibilities may include:

items.text: Managing records, reports and official correspondence.
Supporting accommodation, welfare and station-level services.
Monitoring stock records and material availability.
Coordinating transport, warehousing and movement of authorized supplies.
Supervising assigned personnel and operational support teams.
Maintaining compliance with service procedures and security requirements.
Preparing operational reports and resource plans.
Coordinating with other units to support mission readiness.

blocks.text: The exact duties depend on the officer's branch, rank, posting, training and assigned authority. A Logistics officer is not necessarily responsible for every supply-chain or procurement function at a station.

blocks.text: A degree in Logistics or Aviation Management may be useful for preparation, but it does not automatically confer eligibility or preferential allocation to a particular Ground Duty branch.
Eligibility checks before applying
Verify the current AFCAT notification for:

items.text: Age limits for the intended branch and commission type.
Required educational qualifications and minimum marks.
Written examination and subsequent selection stages.
Medical and physical standards applicable to the branch.
Available vacancies for Administration and Logistics.
Permanent Commission or Short Service Commission availability, where notified.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: Eligibility requirements can change between recruitment cycles. The current official Indian Air Force notification is the authoritative reference.

The AFCAT written examination commonly tests English, general awareness, numerical ability and reasoning or military aptitude. Confirm the current pattern, marking scheme and syllabus before preparing.

By graduation, a competitive applicant should aim to have:

items.text: A degree that meets the current branch requirements.
Strong English, reasoning and numerical aptitude.
Consistent preparation for the AFCAT written examination.
Broad awareness of defence and current affairs.
Evidence of responsibility and initiative through genuine activities.
Basic understanding of administration or logistics.
Verified eligibility for the intended branch and commission type.
Assuming a logistics degree guarantees entry into the Logistics branch.
Ignoring English and reasoning while studying general knowledge.
Preparing only for the written examination.
Memorizing interview answers instead of reflecting on real experiences.
Assuming Administration and Logistics have identical duties.
Believing private certificates can replace official selection or training.
Treating a particular rank or posting as guaranteed.

blocks.text: The strongest preparation combines aptitude, communication, leadership, discipline, analytical ability and professional integrity. Start by confirming the current eligibility rules, then build a consistent examination plan while developing the judgement and teamwork expected of an officer.
